name: factuality
definition: Ensures that every statement referencing the source is correct. According to the prompt, you must 'read the transcript and summary carefully and analyze if any claims are inaccurately attributed to the source or if there are inconsistencies that contradict known facts.' This includes verifying that every claim aligns with the original transcript (Indicator 1) and confirming that no claim contradicts known facts or the transcript itself (Indicator 2).

scoring_guide.5: The summary is riddled with hallucinations or contradictory statements that cannot be traced to the source.
scoring_guide.4: Multiple significant factual errors or misleading claims are present.
scoring_guide.3: There are one or two serious inaccuracies, though much of the summary is correct.
scoring_guide.2: Only minor factual discrepancies or slight unsupported inferences exist.
scoring_guide.1: No false statements or hallucinations; the summary is fully grounded in the source.

example.transcript:
Speaker A: Our team meeting is on Tuesday at 10 AM. The budget for the project is $5,000.
Speaker B: Our main competitor just launched a new product last week.
Speaker A: We might need to adjust our pricing strategy accordingly.

high_score.summary: The team will meet on Tuesday at 10 AM, with a $5,000 budget in place. A competitor has launched a product, prompting a possible pricing strategy update.
high_score.explanation: All details—meeting day/time, budget, competitor launch—accurately match the transcript. No unverified claims are introduced.

low_score.summary: The team will meet tomorrow morning with a $10,000 budget. Competitors are planning to launch in two months.
low_score.explanation: Factual errors contradict the transcript (budget is incorrect, timing of competitor launch is fabricated). This shows multiple hallucinations.
